precepts.text: Moreover, the nations in their wicked conspiracy. The nations got wicked conspiracies, and one of them wicked conspiracies is to destroy us, to wipe out the people of God, the sons of God, the Israelites.
precepts.point: That the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance: so they did that through colonization, through slavery, and through a lot of murders. But also, they doing it through the food and through the medical industry. Through the Food and Drug Administration, they doing the same thing.
precepts.why:
“Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God. For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult.” God has enemies, and God's enemies are the wicked, all nations. A tumult is a loud gathering. “and they that hate thee have lifted up the head”: they that hate God are ruling the earth today.

Wisdom says the same thing: “Moreover, the nations in their wicked conspiracy.” The nations have wicked conspiracies, and one of those wicked conspiracies is to destroy us, to wipe out the people of God, the sons of God, the Israelites.

That is the crafty counsel of Psalms 83, and it goes into many things set up to destroy us as a people. The educational system is crafty counsel. Religious systems are crafty counsel. The medical system was also set up to destroy us, and so was the food system: the FDA.

“They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” They want to kill us. They have been massacring us for hundreds of years: millions of North American Indians over here to this day, millions of Taino Indians and Puerto Ricans, millions of us in Africa. They did it through colonization, through slavery and through a lot of murders, and they are doing the same thing through the food and the medical industry, through the Food and Drug Administration.

precepts.text: The unrighteous is who? Cain. He perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother: when he killed Abel, it wasn't just a tap in the back of the head; he brutally killed Abel in his fury. And Cain got killed too, the same violent way he killed Abel. That's why Rebekah said, why shall I be deprived of you both in one day?
precepts.point: Why should I be deprived also of you both in one day? She knew: if Esau kill Jacob, God will kill Esau. You kill your brother, you're going to die too.

precepts.why:
Isaac told Esau, “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother.” That goes right back to Cain being a fugitive and a vagabond: wandering all around, in lands that don't belong to him, acquiring them by the sword, killing and massacring and holding himself unaccountable. Some say they did not steal the Native Americans' land, they conquered it. What is the difference? After you conquered it, did you give it back? You kept it and gave it to your children, and then gave land to the Irish and British who came afterward and conquered nothing. That is stealing.

“and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”: once David's lineage went off, Esau broke free of our rule and began to conquer. “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing,” and said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” What did Cain do to Abel? He slew him. Nothing new under the sun: the same people doing the same exact thing. Rebekah told Jacob, “thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee”: how evil, to find comfort in killing your own brother.

Wisdom tells what became of Cain: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” The unrighteous is Cain. When he killed Abel it was not a tap on the back of the head; he brutally killed him in his fury. And Cain was killed too, the same violent way he killed Abel.

That is why Rebekah said, “why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” She knew: if Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau. You kill your brother, and you are going to die too.

precepts.text: For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood: he is the cause. Whose evil was responsible for the earth being flooded? Cain's evil. And the sons of God dealt with them: if you're all for Cain now, I'mma kill all of y'all. Likewise today: I promised y'all with the rainbow that I would not flood the earth again. I won't flood it, but I'll burn it.
precepts.point: But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word: the same word preached by who? Noah. Noah preached the same word to the people before the flood, and we're preaching to them before what? Kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men. The same word that was being preached by Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah, to the wicked of our people mingled amongst the other people at the time: the flood came and killed them. That's what we're doing today: here we are back again, preaching to the same wicked sons of God mixed with the same people, before what comes? Fire. It's the exact same thing.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood”: he is the cause. Whose evil was responsible for the earth being flooded? Cain's evil. The heavens that were of old in 2 Peter 3 are Cain's kingdom, the ruling class that was of old, and “the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished”.

The sons of God, Seth's line, went in with Cain's line, and God dealt with them: if you're all for Cain now, I'm going to kill all of you. Then “wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value”: the ark, the little boat the scoffers laughed at, carried Noah through.

Likewise today. Peter says “the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire”. God said, I promised you with the rainbow that I would not flood the earth again. I won't flood it, but I'll burn it. The same cause, the same wicked kingdom ruling, and the same judgment coming, this time by fire, while wisdom directs the course of the righteous who hear the word.

precepts.text: But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother. Cain murdered Abel, and Cain was killed the same way. The judgment catches up.
precepts.point: The fugitive and vagabond speaks of his descendants. Has America paid for its crimes? Have the whites in South Africa paid? In Australia? None of them has paid for their crimes yet.
precepts.why:
Cain said, “Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid”: God was not dealing with him anymore. “and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth.” A fugitive is somebody always on the run, someone who never pays for his crimes. A vagabond is in everybody's land and everybody's home.

But Cain did not escape forever. Wisdom shows he was put to death: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” Cain murdered Abel, and Cain was killed the same way. The judgment caught up with him.

So what did it mean, I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond? It speaks of his descendants. Has America paid for its crimes? Have the whites in South Africa paid? In Australia? None of them has paid for their crimes yet. They have been on the run from justice, living in everybody's land.

That goes with Job 20, read in the same class: “His bones are full of the sin of his youth.” The fugitive has never paid, but as Cain perished in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother, judgment will come on his children. As Job said, “he shall vomit them up again”: everything taken will be restored.

precepts.text: The standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul; the wasteland that smoketh is a testimony to this day.
precepts.point: Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.
precepts.why:
Wisdom “delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.” And the marks of that wickedness remain: “even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.”

Lot’s wife looked back, against the instruction, and “she became a pillar of salt.” That pillar is a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. She was brought out with the righteous, and her look back showed where her heart still was.

You always hear about conspiracy theories; Esau throws that label out any time anybody speaks truth, so the public won't believe you. But when we read the scriptures, God says the nations have wicked conspiracies. They are doing things secretly to destroy our people.

The topic is the secret hands behind South Africa's xenophobia. You see the South Africans rising up, beating people from Nigeria, from Zimbabwe, from Ethiopia, saying get out of my country, and we say these South Africans are foolish; it makes no sense. But when you really examine what's going on, everything you see going on in South Africa, the CIA and Mossad are behind it, and I'm going to show you without a shadow of a doubt.
